intro: Estimate your monthly mortgage payment, total interest, and total cost over the life of the loan.

faqs.q: What's included in this mortgage payment estimate?
faqs.a: This calculator estimates principal and interest only. It does not include property taxes, homeowners insurance, or PMI, which will add to your actual monthly payment.

faqs.q: How does the loan term affect my payment?
faqs.a: A longer term (like 30 years) lowers your monthly payment but increases the total interest paid. A shorter term (like 15 years) raises the monthly payment but saves money over time.

intro: Calculate your estimated monthly car payment based on loan amount, interest rate, and term.

faqs.q: Does this include sales tax or fees?
faqs.a: No, this calculator estimates payments on the loan principal you enter. Add any taxes, title, and registration fees to your loan amount for a more accurate total.

faqs.q: What's a typical auto loan term?
faqs.a: Most auto loans run 36 to 72 months. Shorter terms mean higher monthly payments but less interest paid overall.

intro: See your estimated monthly payment for a personal loan based on amount, rate, and term.

faqs.q: Is this for secured or unsecured loans?
faqs.a: The math works the same for both. Unsecured personal loans typically carry higher interest rates than secured loans.

faqs.q: Can I pay off a personal loan early?
faqs.a: Many lenders allow early payoff, but some charge a prepayment penalty. Check your loan agreement before making extra payments.

intro: Estimate your monthly student loan payment and total repayment cost.

faqs.q: Does this account for income-driven repayment plans?
faqs.a: No, this calculates a standard fixed monthly payment. Income-driven plans adjust your payment based on income and family size instead.

faqs.q: Should I include both federal and private loans?
faqs.a: Calculate them separately since they usually carry different interest rates and repayment terms.
